x: Eric Gebbett our first leg specialist brought us into 8th place just over ½ minute behind Barry Collins who gave Surrey A.C. a lead which they soon lost,never to regain.

Nevertheless, Bill set off with the hope of a miracle but soon proved to himself that Hyman had no intention of being caught and had to content himself with a gain of one place over Barry Collins of Surrey A.C. and at the end we finished a good third.

Barry was one of the last to be dropped by the leaders and as the race wore on looked a good thing for 3rd place, but his last lap was disappointing and young Barry Collins of Surrey A.C. running in his first '20' romped home a clear minute ahead.

Then Barry Collins (Surrey AC) made a break and he managed to hold out just long enough to win. At one time he had a lead of 30y but Mel,finishing very strongly,all but caught the Surrey man on the tape.
The race for the minor positions was a different kettle of fish though,Barry Collins and Bob Holt just managing to get away from Mel Thorpe in the latter stages.
At the start Barry Collins (Surrey) went to the front with Roberts (SLH), Robinson (Achilles) and Gerry North all content to sit in and let him do the early work.

Graham Taylor, who set a magnificent course record of 1hr.39m.47s. the previous year, was unfortunately prevented from turning out by injury, and with the withdrawal by Peter Yates, the race seemed from the start to lie between Scottish international Jim Wright of Tipton, and Barry Collins of Surrey AC.
